data_dictionary.description: Detected archetype vs detected archetype records from decided official matches (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, list #30): one row per archetype and opponent archetype, both directions present, mirrors left out. Team vs team: no source says which four Pokémon were brought. Feeds the Archetypes tab's matchup heatmap.

columns.name: matches
columns.description: Decided matches between the two archetypes' primary teams.

columns.name: wins
columns.description: Matches archetype_key's team won.

columns.name: win_rate
columns.description: wins / matches.

data_dictionary.description: Dashboard-facing experimental archetype summary using primary team assignments only: representative core, usage/player/event support, placement and win-rate context, top extension, and a simple stability label. Neutral core names are intentional; editorial labels are not inferred from composition alone.

How often each Pokémon is shown at team preview, brought, led and Mega Evolved on the Showdown ladder, and how its side does when it is brought versus left at home (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, S3; laundry list #27), from sampled rated replays (pipelines/extract/ showdown_replays.py). One row per regulation, variant (bo1, bo3, or 'all' for both) and Pokémon. Shown and led read every sampled battle; brought, benched and their win rates read complete battles only (both sides revealed all the Pokémon they brought), since a Pokémon brought but never sent in looks benched. The Showdown ladder population, never tournament data: official events aren't played on Showdown. A Mega counts with its base Pokémon (team preview hides the stone).

columns.name: battles
columns.description: Sampled battles in the regulation and variant.

columns.name: complete_battles
columns.description: Of those, the battles where both sides revealed all the Pokémon they brought.

columns.name: shown
columns.description: Sides that showed this Pokémon at team preview.

columns.name: shown_share
columns.description: shown over every sampled side.

columns.name: led
columns.description: Sides that led with it.

columns.name: lead_rate
columns.description: led over shown.

columns.name: complete_shown
columns.description: Sides in complete battles that showed it.

columns.name: brought
columns.description: Of those, sides that brought it (it entered the battle).

columns.name: bring_rate
columns.description: brought over complete_shown.

columns.name: win_rate_brought
columns.description: The side's win rate when it was brought, in decided complete battles.

columns.name: win_rate_benched
columns.description: The side's win rate when it stayed home, in decided complete battles.

columns.name: mega_evolved
columns.description: Sides on which it Mega Evolved.

columns.name: shown_rank
columns.description: Rank by shown, ties broken on pokemon_key.

data_dictionary.description: Showdown ladder checks and counters (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, S2): for each Pokémon, the opponents that most often KO it or force it out, from the battle logs of the regulation's month, all ratings (cutoff 0, the only files that carry them). Pokémon vs Pokémon on the ladder, the only battle-level matchup signal any source publishes; tournament data is team vs team and this is never presented as tournament data. Mirror matches are dropped. Feeds the Pokémon profile's Checks and counters panel.

columns.name: counter_pokemon_key
columns.description: The opponent that checks or counters pokemon_key.

columns.name: encounters
columns.description: Times the pair met and one was KO'd or switched out (Smogon's n). At least 100.

columns.name: ko_or_switch_rate
columns.description: Share of those encounters in which pokemon_key was KO'd or switched out, 0 to 1.

columns.name: counter_rank
columns.description: 1 for pokemon_key's strongest check or counter on that ladder.

data_dictionary.description: The 50 pairs Showdown ladder players most often lead with per regulation and variant (bo1, bo3, 'all'), from sampled rated replays (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, S3; laundry list #27): how often each opens a battle and that side's win rate in decided battles. The Showdown ladder population, never tournament data. A Mega counts with its base Pokémon.

columns.name: pokemon_key_1
columns.description: The pair's first Pokémon (the lower key).

columns.name: pokemon_key_2
columns.description: The pair's second Pokémon.

columns.name: sides_led
columns.description: Sides that opened with the pair.

columns.name: lead_share
columns.description: sides_led over every sampled side that led with two Pokémon.

columns.name: win_rate
columns.description: Those sides' win rate in decided battles.

columns.name: pair_rank
columns.description: Rank by sides_led, ties broken on the keys.

data_dictionary.description: Showdown ladder usage per Pokémon (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, S2, decision D2), from Smogon's monthly statistics: one row per regulation, ladder (variant), rating cutoff and Pokémon, beside the official tournament team share for the same regulation. A separate population, never blended into tournament figures. Feeds the Usage tab's Ladder vs tournament view.

columns.name: month
columns.description: The month the statistics cover (YYYY-MM): the newest one the regulation was in force for at least half of.

columns.name: variant
columns.description: 'bo1' or 'bo3': the Showdown ladder.

columns.name: cutoff
columns.description: Rating cutoff: 1760 weights battles toward players rated above 1760; 0 counts every battle.

columns.name: battles
columns.description: Battles in the month's file: the n behind every share.

columns.name: raw_count
columns.description: Teams it appeared on, unweighted.

columns.name: ladder_usage
columns.description: Weighted share of ladder teams it appeared on, 0 to 1.

columns.name: ladder_rank
columns.description: 1 for the most-used Pokémon on that ladder and cutoff.

columns.name: tournament_team_share
columns.description: Share of the regulation's official tournament teams that brought it (pokemon_usage_by_regulation); null when it was not legal in the latest snapshot.

columns.name: tournament_rank
columns.description: Its usage rank in the regulation's official events.

columns.name: ladder_gap
columns.description: ladder_usage minus tournament_team_share: positive where the ladder plays it more.

data_dictionary.description: The Stat Point spreads Showdown ladder players ran (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, S2, decision D3): per regulation, ladder, rating cutoff and Pokémon, its ten most-run nature and spread combinations. Ladder only: official team sheets publish no spreads, so these never enter a tournament entity, a team sheet or the Builder's sets, and every consumer labels them "Showdown ladder; tournament sheets don't publish spreads".

columns.name: nature
columns.description: The spread's nature.

columns.name: sp_hp
columns.description: Stat Points in HP (sp_atk, sp_def, sp_spa, sp_spd and sp_spe likewise): 66 per Pokémon, at most 32 in one stat.

columns.name: share
columns.description: The spread's share of all the Pokémon's spreads in the file, 0 to 1.

columns.name: spread_rank
columns.description: 1 for the most-run spread.

data_dictionary.description: Legal-pool size per regulation and snapshot_date: legal_pokemon_count (this regulation only) and cumulative_legal_pokemon_count (a naive union of every regulation_code <= this one, within the same snapshot_date). CAVEAT: PokéBase (legality_snapshot's sole source) publishes no removal signal, so cumulative_legal_pokemon_count can only grow across regulations -- it will keep counting a Pokémon that was actually banned in a later regulation, since there's no event to subtract it back out.

Which Mega Stones teams carry (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, E3): one row per Mega form per regulation scope (scope_kind 'regulation', event_id null) and per event (scope_kind 'event'), with its share of the scope's teams. A Mega holder is recorded as its Mega form, so the roster holds this directly.

columns.name: scope_kind
columns.description: 'regulation' (the whole regulation scope, event_id null) or 'event' (one event's teams).

columns.name: scope_code
columns.description: The regulation ("m-c", ..., or 'all') for a 'regulation' row; the event's regulation for an 'event' row.

columns.name: item_name
columns.description: The Mega Stone that form holds (its most common held item).

columns.name: team_count
columns.description: Teams in the scope carrying this Mega form.

columns.name: scope_team_count
columns.description: Teams in the scope: the regulation's (or 'all') or the event's.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: team_count over scope_team_count: the share of teams carrying this Mega.

data_dictionary.description: One row per Limitless online tournament (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, S1): name, date, regulation, the platform's entrant count, how many published team sheets it contributes, decided pairings and the winning team. Online events are their own population and never appear in tournament_event_summary. Feeds the Events tab's online list, which links out to play.limitlesstcg.com.

columns.name: event_id
columns.description: The event's tournament_event.event_id ("LP-<tournament id>").

columns.name: regulation_code
columns.description: The Champions regulation the tournament was played under.

columns.name: registered_player_count
columns.description: Entrants as the platform reports them, published list or not.

columns.name: team_count
columns.description: Players whose team sheet was published; online usage rests on these.

columns.name: match_count
columns.description: Decided pairings, Swiss and top cut.

columns.name: winner_count
columns.description: Teams holding placing 1. Above 1 the platform shared first place, and the winner_* columns are null rather than a guess.

columns.name: source_url
columns.description: The tournament's standings page on play.limitlesstcg.com.

columns.name: recency_rank
columns.description: 1 for the regulation's newest online tournament, counting back.

data_dictionary.description: Upcoming Limitless online tournaments of the regulation in force (and one registered to start within 30 days), from the newest limitless_play_upcoming snapshot (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, list #31): one row per tournament, from three hours before the snapshot was read on. Organiser-run online events, never official ones; no player appears. Feeds the Events tab's "Upcoming online tournaments" list, which shows local times and drops tournaments that have started.

columns.name: starts_at_utc
columns.description: Scheduled start, ISO-8601 UTC ("2026-10-23T12:00:00Z").

columns.name: platform
columns.description: 'Switch' (the game) or 'Showdown' (Pokémon Showdown).

columns.name: registrations
columns.description: Players registered when the page was read.

columns.name: player_cap
columns.description: The registration cap, empty when the organiser set none.

columns.name: registration_open
columns.description: Whether registration was open when the page was read.

data_dictionary.description: A player's team-vs-team record against each detected archetype they faced, per regulation_scope (each regulation plus 'all'), from decided Masters matches; rows with fewer than 2 matches in their scope are dropped.

columns.name: player_id
columns.description: The player.

columns.name: regulation_scope
columns.description: A regulation code, or 'all' for every Champions regulation together.

columns.name: opponent_archetype_key
columns.description: The opponent team's primary archetype.

columns.name: matches_played
columns.description: Decided matches against teams of that archetype.

data_dictionary.description: One row per player, derived at build time from tournament_team_results: name and country as the source spells them, teams on record (one per event), best finish and regulations played.

Player-grain half of backlog.md #7 ("does this player have a signature Pokémon," across their full history): one row per player_id x pokemon_key they've fielded, restricted to the current legal pool. player_usage_share is this Pokémon's fraction of the player's own total legal-pool roster appearances across every team of theirs on record; player_pokemon_rank 1 is their most-played Pokémon. player_team_count (distinct teams this player has fielded) is a sample-size signal alongside the rank.

Ability drill-down for the Pokémon Profile tab's Ability section: usage count and ability_share (that count's fraction of the Pokémon's own total ability rows) per Pokémon x ability, restricted to the current legal pool, ranked within each Pokémon, with short_effect joined from ability_detail.

Item and ability build concentration (backlog.md #14): a Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (sum of squared shares) over pokemon_item_usage.item_share and pokemon_ability_usage.ability_share per Pokémon -- HHI near 1 means usage is concentrated on a single locked-in item/ability, near 0 means usage is spread across several contested choices. item_count/ability_count is how many distinct items/abilities were observed at all.

Denormalized per-Pokémon profile for the Speed Tiers and Team Builder dashboard views: one row per currently legal Pokémon with its Champions-format base stats (including speed) plus nullable overall usage_count/usage_share/win_rate/record_count. max_investment_speed (backlog.md #16) is the Level-50 Speed stat under the standard "max speed investment" competitive convention (32 Stat Points, a beneficial Stat Alignment, IVs fixed at 31 in Champions) rather than raw base speed -- see pokemon_speed_tiers below for the full modified-speed bracket table built on top of it.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: Share of the partition's teams that brought this Pokémon (usage_count over the team count): the headline usage metric (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, V1), the unit the official usage card, Pikalytics and Smogon report.

data_dictionary.description: Day 2 conversion (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, E1): each Pokémon's share of the teams that reached Day 2 or the top cut against its share of the whole field at the same events, and the ratio between them. Official events with RK9 pairings; Day 2 and the top cut are read off the round structure (int_event_phases). Two grains: scope_kind 'event' (event_id set, scope_code the event's regulation) and 'regulation' (scope_code a regulation or 'all', event_id null). Feeds event pages' conversion table and the Top 12 board's Day 2 switch.

columns.name: phase
columns.description: 'day2' or 'top_cut'.

columns.name: team_count
columns.description: Teams in the phase that brought the Pokémon.

columns.name: phase_team_count
columns.description: Teams in the phase: the share's n.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: team_count / phase_team_count.

columns.name: field_team_count
columns.description: Every team at the same events: the field's n.

columns.name: field_team_share
columns.description: The Pokémon's share of the whole field at the same events.

columns.name: conversion
columns.description: team_share / field_team_share; 1.0 means it reached the phase at its field rate.

columns.name: is_reliable
columns.description: Both sides have at least 100 teams (the What changed panel's floor). When false, show counts but not the ratio.

data_dictionary.description: Usage of each Pokémon at each Champions event against its regulation's average (share of roster slots), including Pokémon absent from the event. Feeds an event page's over- and under-performers and the event-window filter.

columns.name: event_id
columns.description: The event.

columns.name: pokemon_key
columns.description: The Pokémon.

columns.name: event_usage_share
columns.description: usage_count / event_slot_count.

columns.name: regulation_usage_share
columns.description: The Pokémon's usage share across the whole regulation.

columns.name: usage_share_delta
columns.description: event_usage_share - regulation_usage_share.

columns.name: event_team_share
columns.description: Share of the event's teams that brought the Pokémon, usage_count over event_team_count.

columns.name: regulation_team_share
columns.description: The Pokémon's team share across the whole regulation.

columns.name: team_share_delta
columns.description: event_team_share minus regulation_team_share: how much more (or less) the field brought it than usual.

data_dictionary.description: Real head-to-head records per (pokemon_key, opponent_pokemon_key), built on tournament_match (RK9 pairings, backlog.md #27): how often teams fielding the first Pokémon beat teams fielding the second, with a 95% Wilson lower bound since head-to-head samples are small. CAVEAT, and it must be surfaced wherever this is displayed: the grain is team vs team, NOT Pokémon vs Pokémon. RK9 publishes no per-battle log naming which Pokémon were brought (VGC brings 4 of 6) or which defeated which, so a row reads "teams with A beat teams with B this often", never "A beats B". Pairs are mirrored, and scoped to Masters, to decided matches, and to the current legal pool.

Item drill-down for the Pokémon Profile tab's Items section (top 5 shown in the dashboard UI): usage count and item_share (that count's fraction of the Pokémon's own total item rows) per Pokémon x item, restricted to the current legal pool, ranked within each Pokémon, with short_effect joined from item_detail. Replaces the old combined pokemon_build_usage mart (see pokemon_ability_usage below for the other half of that split).

Each Pokémon's name in Japanese, Spanish, French and German (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, Q4): one row per pokemon_key and language, for the dashboard's name-language switch. Names only; Portuguese uses the English names.

columns.name: language
columns.description: ja, es, fr or de.

columns.name: localised_name
columns.description: The Pokémon's name in the language.

columns.name: name_rule
columns.description: species, pokeapi_form, mega, form_label, regional, gender or fallback: whether PokéAPI published the name or it was composed (data/staging/pokeapi_names.schema.json).

data_dictionary.description: One row per Pokémon: overall head-to-head win rate plus its best and worst matchups, chosen by Wilson lower bound over a minimum of 10 matches (a raw win-rate extreme is always a 1-0 record). Inherits pokemon_head_to_head's team-vs-team caveat exactly.

Move drill-down for the Pokémon Profile tab's Moves section (top 15 shown in the dashboard UI) and the Matchup tab's damage calculator: usage count and move_share (that count's fraction of the Pokémon's own total move rows) per Pokémon x move, unnesting tournament_team_member's pipe-delimited moves list, restricted to the current legal pool, ranked within each Pokémon, with move_type/power/accuracy/category/priority/pp/short_effect joined from move_detail.

Nature drill-down per Pokémon x nature (usage_count, nature_share, usage_rank within the Pokémon), restricted to the current legal pool and partitioned by regulation_scope. Feeds the Pokémon Profile's most-common-set card.

Placement-weighted usage (backlog.md #8): distinguishes "popular" from "successful" using tournament_team.placement (lower is better). top_cut_usage_count/top_cut_usage_share use a hard top-8 cutoff; placement_weighted_score/weighted_usage_share use a continuous inverse-placement (1/placement) weight per appearance instead.

columns.name: top_cut_team_share
columns.description: Share of the scope's top-8 teams that brought the Pokémon.

columns.name: weighted_team_share
columns.description: The Pokémon's teams' summed 1/placement weight over every placed team's: team share where a win counts fully and a 10th place a tenth.

data_dictionary.description: Regulation-to-regulation "what changed" feed: per Pokémon, usage share/rank and win rate in a regulation beside the regulation before it (consecutive pairs from the champions_regulations seed), with deltas, an is_new_to_format flag (not legal in the previous regulation) and both regulations' team counts as sample size. Needs no extraction-snapshot history (docs/upgrade-plan-2026q4.md, A4).

columns.name: usage_share_delta
columns.description: The same delta over roster-slot shares, about one sixth of team_share_delta.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: This regulation's team share (see pokemon_usage_summary.team_share).

columns.name: previous_team_share
columns.description: The previous regulation's team share.

columns.name: team_share_delta
columns.description: team_share minus previous_team_share, in share points: the headline 'What changed' delta.

data_dictionary.description: Real sets per Pokémon: the item, ability, nature and four moves that appeared together on one team sheet (set_level 'full'), plus a looser 'core' level grouping item + ability + the set's three most common moves. Top 5 per Pokémon, regulation scope and level, ranked by team_count then Wilson lower bound. share_of_pokemon divides by all of the Pokémon's roster slots, so shares sum to at most 1.

columns.name: pokemon_key
columns.description: The Pokémon running the set.

columns.name: set_level
columns.description: 'full' (exact set) or 'core' (item + ability + top 3 moves).

columns.name: moves
columns.description: Pipe-delimited, sorted alphabetically: four for 'full', three for 'core'.

columns.name: team_count
columns.description: Roster slots (one per team) that ran the set.

columns.name: share_of_pokemon
columns.description: team_count / every roster slot of the Pokémon in the scope.

columns.name: wilson_lower_bound
columns.description: 95% Wilson lower bound on the teams' combined win rate.

columns.name: example_team_id
columns.description: One team that ran the set verbatim.

data_dictionary.description: Speed-tier bracket mart (backlog.md #16): modified Speed under the format's common competitive scenarios, built on top of pokemon_champions_profile.max_investment_speed. plus_one_speed/ scarf_speed (x1.5) and plus_two_speed/tailwind_speed (x2.0) are numerically identical pairs kept as separately-named columns since they answer different real questions (a stat-stage boost vs. an item vs. a team-wide field effect); scarf_tailwind_speed (x3.0) covers the common scarfed-Pokémon-under-Tailwind combination. The multipliers themselves are fixed game-mechanics constants, the same treatment already given to app.js's SPEED_TIERS thresholds and matchup.js's TYPE_CHART.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: Share of the partition's teams that brought this Pokémon (usage_count over the team count): the headline usage metric (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, V1), the unit the official usage card, Pikalytics and Smogon report.

data_dictionary.description: Canonical three-Pokemon Champions team cores. Each row is one pokemon_key_a < pokemon_key_b < pokemon_key_c triple with distinct team/player/event support, observed and expected team share, three-way lift, constituent pair-lift summaries, placement/win-rate context, and support/lift ranks.

Team-core drill-down (docs/prd.md's "Drill-down by Pokémon, team core, move, and item usage"): co-occurrence usage count and partner_share (that count's fraction of the Pokémon's own total co-occurrence count across all partners) per Pokémon x partner Pokémon pair appearing on the same tournament team, restricted to the current legal pool, ranked within each anchor Pokémon by co-occurrence count. Symmetric: each unordered pair appears twice (once per anchor direction) so either Pokémon in the pair can be the drill-down's selected anchor.

Team synergy beyond raw co-occurrence (backlog.md #9): lift per Pokémon x partner Pokémon pair -- the ratio of a pair's observed team co-occurrence rate to the rate expected if the two Pokémon were paired independently of their individual popularity. lift > 1 is a genuine pairing; lift < 1 is paired less than chance. Built on top of pokemon_team_core_usage's mirrored pairs. pair_team_count is exposed alongside lift since lift is noisy at low pair counts.

Country-grain half of backlog.md #7 ("which regions favor which archetypes"): usage x player_country cross-tab, restricted to the current legal pool and to roster rows with a reported player_country (optional in the source). usage_share/ country_usage_rank are computed within each player_country partition, mirroring pokemon_usage_by_regulation's usage-x-dimension pattern.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: Share of the country's teams that brought the Pokémon, over country_team_count.

columns.name: country_team_count
columns.description: Teams whose player reported this country.

data_dictionary.description: Usage over time from tournament_event.event_date (backlog.md #6): usage count/share/rank per Pokémon x event_date, partitioned by event_date -- a real meta-over-time view that doesn't need multiple extraction snapshots (Blocker A), since it trends across tournaments actually played instead of across re-extraction dates.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: Share of that date's teams that brought the Pokémon.

data_dictionary.description: Usage x regulation cross-tab (backlog.md #12): every Pokémon legal under each regulation (legality_snapshot at the latest snapshot_date) with its usage in events played under that regulation, 0 if unused. usage_share/usage_rank are computed within each regulation_code. A true temporal slice since tournament_event gained regulation_code (docs/upgrade-plan-2026q4.md, A2).

columns.name: usage_share
columns.description: Share of all roster slots (six per team), about one sixth of team_share. Kept for tooltips and local queries; team_share is the headline.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: Share of the partition's teams that brought this Pokémon (usage_count over the team count): the headline usage metric (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, V1), the unit the official usage card, Pikalytics and Smogon report.

data_dictionary.description: Total tournament-roster usage per Pokémon (restricted to the current legal pool), ranked descending, with an event_tier filter dimension: one overall row per Pokémon (event_tier is null) plus one row per tournament tier it appears in, each ranked within its own event_tier partition.

columns.name: usage_count
columns.description: Teams (and roster slots: a Pokémon appears at most once per team) that brought this Pokémon in the partition.

columns.name: usage_share
columns.description: Share of all roster slots (six per team), about one sixth of team_share. Kept for tooltips and local queries; team_share is the headline.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: Share of the partition's teams that brought this Pokémon (usage_count over the team count): the headline usage metric (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, V1), the unit the official usage card, Pikalytics and Smogon report.

columns.name: scope_team_count
columns.description: Teams in the (regulation_scope, event_tier) partition, team_share's denominator. Counts every team, including any whose members fall outside the current legal pool.

data_dictionary.description: Win-rate-proxy KPI per Pokémon: total wins/losses and win_rate aggregated from tournament_team's reported record_wins/record_losses across every roster slot that included the Pokémon, restricted to the current legal pool and to teams with a reported record. wilson_lower_bound/wilson_rank (backlog.md #13) are a 95% Wilson score confidence interval lower bound and its rank, which order small-sample win rates more honestly than raw win_rate does (a 100% win rate over 3 matches no longer outranks 62% over 200).

Cross-source validation, one row per event covered by both MunchStats and Limitless: how often the two independently agree on a player's six Pokémon. exact_agreement_rate is whole-roster agreement, slot_agreement_rate is per-slot. The event join is real rather than heuristic — Limitless links out to the same event on RK9, and MunchStats reuses RK9's event ids. covered_players is stated because the comparison spans Limitless' day-2 cut, not the full field. This mart earned its keep immediately: it reported 0% exact agreement on first run, which is what surfaced the Mega representation difference now handled by limitless_mega_item_to_pokeapi_form (see int_limitless_mapped.sql).

Top Teams tab's "Converged lists" feed: one row per canonical Limitless team-list id, ranked by how many distinct players fielded that same six-Pokémon composition (player_count), with tournament_count, best_placement, first_seen_date and the full roster (pokemon_keys, pipe-delimited in slot order). Surfaces the team_list/team_list_member layer, which no other mart reads. Scoping note: Limitless is a Champions-only source and this mart's grain is team_list_member, so it does not (and cannot) route through int_champions_roster — see the model header. Coverage caveat: Limitless publishes the day-2 cut only (~93 distinct Pokémon against 203 in the full Champions roster), so this describes what converged at the top of the field, not the meta.

Full sheets (item, ability, nature, moves per slot) for the 60 most converged Limitless team lists, so Top Teams' "Use this team" loads a converged list into the Builder with real sets. One row per list x slot.

columns.name: team_list_id
columns.description: The Limitless team list.

data_dictionary.description: The share of teams carrying zero, one, two (or, rarely, more) Mega forms, per regulation scope and per event, the second half of the Mega usage panel (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, E3).

columns.name: mega_count
columns.description: How many Mega forms a team's sheet lists.

columns.name: team_share
columns.description: The share of the scope's teams with exactly mega_count Megas; the rows of one scope sum to 1.

data_dictionary.description: Top Teams tab's leaderboard feed: one row per tournament_team with a reported win/loss record, ranked by win_rate, with event context and full member roster (pokemon_keys, pipe-delimited in slot order).

One row per Champions event: name, date, tier, regulation, how many teams and players it has on record, how many reported a W-L record, how many decided Masters matches RK9 published, and the winning team. Feeds the event index, each event page's header and the events/teams sample-size KPI.

columns.name: event_id
columns.description: The event's tournament_event.event_id.

columns.name: regulation_code
columns.description: The Champions regulation the event was played under.

columns.name: team_count
columns.description: Teams with at least one Champions roster row.

columns.name: player_count
columns.description: Distinct players with a team at the event.

columns.name: recorded_team_count
columns.description: Teams that reported a W-L record.

columns.name: match_count
columns.description: Decided Masters matches in RK9 pairings (0 when RK9 has none).

columns.name: winner_pokemon_keys
columns.description: The placement-1 team's Pokémon, pipe-delimited in slot order.

columns.name: recency_rank
columns.description: 1 for the regulation's newest event, counting back.

data_dictionary.description: One row per Champions team: event, player (as the source spells the name), placement, W-L record, its six Pokémon, whether the sheet is fully reported (six Pokémon, each with item, ability, nature and four moves) and its primary detected archetype. data_dictionary.description: Full team sheets (item, ability, nature, moves per slot) for every top-16 finish at a Champions event and every team on the top_tournament_teams leaderboard: the teams a reader can copy for Showdown or load into the Builder. One row per team x slot. No EV or IV columns: team sheets don't publish them.

columns.name: team_id
columns.description: The team's tournament_team.team_id.

columns.name: pokemon_key
columns.description: The Pokémon in this slot.

columns.name: moves
columns.description: Up to four moves, pipe-delimited as the sheet lists them.

data_dictionary.description: The single-elimination bracket of each official event with RK9 pairings (docs/upgrade-plan-2027q2.md, E2): one row per top-cut match, each side with its player, placement and six Pokémon. Team vs team: no source names the Pokémon brought to a game.

columns.name: bracket_round
columns.description: 1 for the top cut's first round, counting up to the final.

columns.name: top_cut_size
columns.description: Players in the top cut: its first round's slots less the byes (13 in a 16-slot bracket with three byes).

columns.name: bracket_size
columns.description: Slots in the top cut's first round (16, or 32).

columns.name: round_label
columns.description: 'Round of 32', 'Round of 16', 'Quarterfinals', 'Semifinals' or 'Final'.

columns.name: vod_url
columns.description: A video of the match from the curated featured_match_vods seed (S5), with `&t=<n>s` when it starts partway in; empty for a match with none.

data_dictionary.description: Every Masters round each top-cut team played (docs/upgrade-plan- 2027q2.md, E2), Day 1 to the end, with the opponent and the result: the path an event page shows when a bracket player is clicked. Team vs team.

columns.name: phase
columns.description: 'Day 1', 'Day 2' or 'Top cut'.

columns.name: result
columns.description: W, L, T or Bye, for this team.

data_dictionary.description: Top-16 finishes from tournament_team_results, derived at build time for Top Teams, event pages and a profile's Teams view.

release_tables.description: Canonical identity table for Pokémon and form references.
Time-sliced legal status for the Champions pool.
Normalized tournament metadata: official events from MunchStats, and Limitless online tournaments as their own population (event_tier 'Online').
One row per Pokémon on a normalized tournament team.

One row per played match: who faced whom, in which round, and who won, sourced from RK9 pairings (official events) and Limitless pairings (online tournaments, division 'Online'). Grain is team vs team, not Pokémon vs Pokémon — no source publishes a per-battle Pokémon-level log.
One row per canonical Limitless team-list id: a team composition identity reused across the players and events that fielded it. Covers the day-2 cut only.
One row per Pokémon on a canonical team list, with held item, ability, nature and moves. No EV/IV spread: official team sheets do not publish one.

Image manifest for Pokémon/form references. One row per pokemon_key per image_kind: 128x128 menu_sprite from Bulbagarden Archives (the dense-UI asset) and 512x512 home_render from PokéAPI's sprite repository (the hero asset). Primary key is the composite pokemon_asset_key (<pokemon_key>::<image_kind>) — pokemon_key alone is deliberately non-unique.
